alex thompson: quick q — what's the recommended way to manage multiple CLI profiles and auth for the redwood CLI when scripting? thinking: hosted vs private tokens, CI usage, and where creds actually live on disk for mac/linux/windows

maya singh: short answer: use profiles + env vars for CI. redwood CLI stores a small config in ~/.redwood/config and keeps credential blobs in ~/.redwood/credentials by default on *nix. on mac/windows we prefer OS keyring when available (mac keychain, windows credential manager). if keyring missing it falls back to the credentials file.

maya singh: common commands I use:
```
# create a profile that points at private deployment
redwood profile create --name private-staging --endpoint https://private.example.com --token-file ~/.secrets/redwood-staging.token

# list profiles
redwood profile ls

# activate for current shell
redwood profile use private-staging
```

sam wu: for CI we don't call interactive login. put token into your secret manager and expose as env var in pipeline: REDWOOD_API_KEY. then call the CLI with the env var, e.g.
```bash
REDWOOD_API_KEY="$REDWOOD_API_KEY" redwood call --model gpt-redwood --input file.json --output out.json
```
This avoids writing credentials to disk in CI.

alex thompson: good — what about token rotation? want to rotate without restarting jobs.

maya singh: rotate token in secret manager and your jobs should pick up new env value on next run. For long-running processes, you can use `redwood auth refresh --profile private-staging --token-env REDWOOD_API_KEY` to re-read env-var or `redwood auth reload` which will attempt to re-load keyring/creds file. We also support short-lived tokens via `--expires-in` for automated workflows.

jordan lee: small gotcha: streaming output from the CLI can be block-buffered in some CI runners (it prints progressively locally but batched in Docker). If you rely on streaming, use `stdbuf -oL` or run with `--no-buffer` (CLI flag) or ensure your runner supports TTY. Also node child_process stdout may buffer; use `spawn` with stdio: 'inherit' or pipe and manually flush.

sam wu: submitting a tiny PR that adds `--profile` flag to the `redwood call` wrapper in tools/ci.sh — can someone review? pinging @maya @jordan for lgtm.

maya singh: looking now. quick review: please add a fallback to check REDWOOD_API_KEY before reading profile file and document that in README. also add a `--json` output mode so scripts can parse responses reliably instead of grepping the pretty stream.

ci-bot: build passed: tools-ci #342 (linux, bash 5.1) :white_check_mark:

alex thompson: thanks all — I'll update the runbook docs about where creds live and the recommended patterns (env var for CI, keyring for dev, profile+token-file for ad-hoc). if anyone has short examples I can paste in the runbook that would be great.
